question: Does baseline miniaturization define a general human recoverability boundary?

evidence.design: serial scalp biopsy follicular counts; men randomized to finasteride 1 mg or placebo for 12 months
evidence.unit_strength: region/biopsy-level counts rather than same-follicle longitudinal identity
evidence.reported_pattern: terminal counts increased and miniaturized counts decreased more with finasteride in men, interpreted as evidence compatible with some reversal of miniaturization
evidence.HF01_use: group/region-level longitudinal compatibility; not same-follicle recoverability

evidence.design: 13 men, 24-month phototrichogram study after short no-treatment baseline, then finasteride; mapped hair sites
evidence.unit_strength: individual mapped-hair/site dynamics stronger than aggregate biopsy counts; small uncontrolled cohort
evidence.reported_pattern: of 113 baseline miniaturized hairs <=30 um, 79 remained miniature after two years and most remaining mapped sites did not show terminal hairs; moderate improvement was attributed mainly to reactivation of deficient terminal follicles
evidence.HF01_use: human longitudinal defeater against assuming finasteride response means vellus-to-terminal reconversion; too small/uncontrolled for a universal threshold

evidence.design: hair-to-hair matched phototrichograms; 33-man 24-week randomized double-blind placebo-controlled 0.45 mg sublingual-minoxidil trial plus 12-person open-label higher-dose extension
evidence.unit_strength: individual hairs are linked across time, but hair-level results were pooled across patients within treatment/diameter strata
evidence.reported_pattern: 0.45 mg did not increase mean fibre diameter; 1.35 mg and 4.05 mg extension groups showed dose-associated increases, with larger/intermediate-to-terminal baseline fibres showing the largest increases
evidence.HF01_use: strong evidence that actuator dose and baseline fibre state interact with observed response; higher-dose inference is not from the randomized placebo-controlled arm

conflict_resolution: Do not infer a universal miniaturization irreversibility threshold from any one study.
Do not combine different actuators/doses into one control-gain curve.
Distinguish same-follicle/fibre tracking from region-level counts.
Preserve participant/donor hierarchy even when individual hairs are tracked; hair count is not independent human n.
Treat fibre diameter as an output/proxy, not a direct measurement of P, E, M or F_hyst.
model_update: Define recoverability surfaces and any FRK candidate conditional on a declared actuator u: g(z,u), FRK(u). A knee for one actuator/dose is not a universal follicle state boundary.
claim_boundary: The ledger documents conflicting human longitudinal response patterns. It does not rank treatments or recommend finasteride/minoxidil use.
